title: The Problem analyst in a built project's chat: a changed problem shown before and after, checked against the table, confirmed as a version
request: Start step 1: the problem analyst in the built chat (connect the Home orchestrator to problem understanding).
spec: Once a project was built, nothing in its chat could handle 'the outcome should be another column', 'we score at signup' or 'within 60 days, not 30'; the orchestrator's team only read records and improved the model.
plan: A fifth specialist, the Problem analyst, with tools show_problem, propose_problem_change and confirm_problem_change in the scope 'home'
A proposal is built from the draft's problem card with the changes, checked with dclab_core.meet against the project's data card, its consequences by rule
Nothing changes in the built project; a confirmed change is kept as a version of the problem on the chat
Rules read the change from the words when no model serves; the model gets the problem and the table's column names
Capture: the orchestrator's turns kept by the store; its agents registered with their capture tasks

decisions.decision: A changed problem never edits the built project.
decisions.why: A new outcome or moment is another problem: its results need a fresh held-back split; the old one was read for the first problem.

decisions.decision: The fit with the table is the existing meet check, and a blocking mismatch cannot be confirmed by a yes.
decisions.why: One rule for problem and data everywhere; an identifier as the outcome is refused, whoever proposes it.

decisions.decision: One change is pending at a time; a yes confirms it, whatever the model names it.
decisions.why: Live: the model passed a description instead of the id and the first confirmation failed.

decisions.decision: Confirmed versions add up; a proposal that replaces an unconfirmed one says so.
decisions.why: Live: a later proposal was compared with the problem as built and silently dropped the earlier unconfirmed change.

change: dclab_rnd/draft/orchestrator.py (the analyst's tools, problem_change rules, the situation's problem and columns, declining), dclab_rnd/prompts/home_orchestrator.md, dclab_rnd/models/settings.py (what the purpose may see), dclab_rnd/store/tasks.py and keepers/standard.py and shapers.py (the orchestrator agents and their turns kept), tests/test_home_orchestrator.py, scripts/home_orchestrator_live.py (the problem conversation).

findings.defect: A built chat could not take a changed problem.
findings.scenario: The person says the outcome should be another column.
findings.cause: The understanding agents ended at the build.
findings.fix: The Problem analyst's three tools and their rules.

findings.defect: An identifier proposed as the outcome was not flagged.
findings.scenario: A draft without a table profile; the target customer_id.
findings.cause: card_of sets the outcome column only when the draft's profile lists it.
findings.fix: The named outcome and time column are put on the checked card directly.

findings.defect: The rules picked the old outcome as the new one.
findings.scenario: 'the outcome should be demo_requested, not converted_this_month'.
findings.cause: The longest column named won; the old one was longer.
findings.fix: A column after not, instead of, rather than or from is the old one.

findings.defect: 'no, the prediction is made when ...' was read as declining.
findings.scenario: A correction that starts with no.
findings.cause: NO was checked before the change; the moment pattern missed 'is made when'.
findings.fix: The change is read first; the moment pattern takes is, are, made; after a no, the rest of the sentence is planned.

findings.scenario: The model named the change in words.
findings.cause: confirm required the pending change's id.
findings.fix: One change is pending at a time: a yes confirms it.

findings.defect: A later proposal was compared with the problem as built and dropped an unconfirmed change silently.
findings.scenario: Outcome confirmed, then a horizon, then a moment.
findings.cause: Proposals read the built problem; a new proposal replaced the pending one without a word.
findings.fix: Confirmed versions keep the whole problem and add up; a replaced proposal is said on the card.

findings.defect: The orchestrator's turns were not kept by the store, and its two agents had no capture tasks.
findings.scenario: The store's conductor over a workspace with built chats.
findings.cause: home_orchestrator/ had no claim; AGENT_TASKS lacked home.project and home.project.rules.
findings.fix: A claim and a shaper for home_orchestrator/; the two agents' tasks.

findings.defect: A refusal started what it refused.
findings.scenario: 'no, don't improve it' queued the improvement job; 'cancel, don't adopt it' adopted.
findings.cause: After a no, the rest was planned again with its own negation stripped.
findings.fix: The rest is read only after a bare no or nope, and never when it is itself a refusal.

findings.defect: Ordinary requests were taken as a changed problem.
findings.scenario: 'plot the predictions in a different color', 'change the 30-day features', 'why does it predict wrong on the plan column'.
findings.cause: Loose words (different, wrong, predict), any column named, any N-day.
findings.fix: An outcome only right after an outcome phrase, a horizon only beside a word of the outcome and never before 'features'; the which-part fallback after every other reading.

findings.defect: A change could be confirmed without the person's yes.
findings.scenario: A proposal left pending, then a model's confirm after a yes meant for something else.
findings.cause: confirm ignored whether the person was asked; a pending change never expired.
findings.fix: Confirm needs the offer of the turn before; an unanswered proposal expires.

findings.defect: A confirmation could write an older proposal over a newer one.
findings.scenario: A proposal stored between the read and the update.
findings.cause: The value confirmed was read before store.update.
findings.fix: The stored proposal is read again inside the update and confirmed only if it is the same one.

measurements.name: The problem conversation on a copy of the owner's lead project (Claude Sonnet 5.5)
measurements.gate: each turn calls the analyst's tool it must, never the Experimenter; the built project unchanged
measurements.result: run 1: 7/7 (EUR 0.067) with two behaviours fixed after; run 2: 7/7 (EUR 0.067), the project's solution unchanged, one version confirmed; run 3 after the review: 7/7 (EUR 0.062)
limits: seven turns written by the builder, one project
the sealed journeys of model roles were not run: this is the orchestrator's purpose, not the roles'

measurements.name: The same conversation, rules only
measurements.gate: each turn calls the tool it must and none it must not
measurements.result: 7/7 after P3 and P4; after the review: 7/7, and the first conversation 9/9
limits: the rules read three parts (outcome, moment, horizon); unit and kind changes need the model or the words of a column

outcome: In a built chat the person can change the problem; the analyst shows what would change and whether it fits the table, and keeps the confirmed problem as a version while the built project stays as it is.
lessons: Before trusting a 'longest match', ask which mention is the old value: words like not and instead mark it.
A new agent needs its capture registered, or the store loses its records.
risks: A confirmed version is not built yet: step 2 (the Solution planner) turns it into a new project version.
